what: A substitution that reverts --select-cell's focus to "only creatures of ownership" — the exact defect Issue #373 opened about — has to redden criterion 2's check on (16,7). It does.

mutant.appliedAtCommit: a7dff80 (this Issue's own checkpoint 1-4 commit; the mutant was built, run and then reverted on top of it, never itself committed)

before.note: The fixed code, evidence/373-focus.json's criterion2 block.
before.controlFeedback: (16,7): 1 of 2 standing here; click the cell again for the next one.

reddened.what: Criterion 2 ("the frame with the raider under focus") is exactly what this mutant breaks: --select-cell 16,7 answers "nothing stands there" although two raiders stand on it, reproducing verbatim the failure Issue #373 measured on the pre-fix codebase ("--select-cell не дотягивается вовсе... заполняет _selectedCreatureId только из state.Creatures").
reddened.howNotJustAsserted: Both runs print the identical canonical checksum, so the mutant is presentation-only — it could not have been caught by any Simulation-layer test. The bottom feedback line is the one pixel region (bbox [16,589]-[319,601], measured with PIL ImageChops.difference, same method as evidence/373-focus.json's pixelDiff) that changes between the fixed screenshot and the mutant one; that is the check the mutant reddens, and it is legible from the printed JSON alone without opening the PNG.

revert.confirmedBy: dotnet build src/DungeonFortress.Game/DungeonFortress.Game.csproj after restoring the was line reported 0 warnings, 0 errors, and rerunning the before command reproduced controlFeedback "(16,7): 1 of 2 standing here..." and checksum f8e26b05... again.
revert.note: The mutant was written, built, run and reverted after evidence/373-hover.json, 373-focus.json and 373-body-index.json's commands had already been committed (a7dff80), per Issue #373's own instruction that a mutant only runs after the checkpoint it could otherwise erase is safe.
